transcript.text: Bosch integrated dishwasher showing E:15 and the pump keeps running. Model SMV4HTX31E. I've turned it off and on, still there

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. E:15 on Bosch dishwashers is a safety feature called Aquastop. It means water has been detected in the bottom base pan of the machine (either from an internal leak or a spill), and the system has triggered the drain pump to run continuously to prevent flooding. The most common cause is simply that the anti-flood float switch in the base has become wet. To fix this, you must remove the water from that tray. Please pull the dishwasher out carefully (ensure the water supply tap is turned off first), place towels underneath, and tilt the machine back to drain any standing water from the bottom into a bucket. Once empty, dry the area thoroughly with kitchen roll. After doing this, plug it back in and turn the water on. Does the E:15 code clear?

I can't pull it out or tilt it, it's fully integrated under the worktop and the kitchen plinth is glued at the ends. I can see a bit of water shine in the base tray through a gap with a torch though. Any other way to get it out?

I understand you can't move the machine. Unfortunately, E:15 means the anti-flood switch in the base pan has detected water, and that switch is located at the very bottom of the appliance. If we cannot remove that water from the tray, the error will not clear and the pump will continue to run. However, before calling an engineer, we should check if the issue can be resolved by clearing a blockage inside the tub that might be causing the leak or overflow. Please switch off and unplug the dishwasher again for safety. Remove the lower rack, then twist and lift out the main cylindrical filter at the bottom of the tub. Check if it is blocked with food or debris. Also, look into the sump (the hole where the filter was) to see if there is standing water above the normal level (a small cupful is normal; more than that suggests a blockage or leak). Let me know what you find.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the filter is" — The filter sits in the base of the dishwasher, usually under the bottom spray arm. Twist it out anticlockwise and rinse it under a tap. Typical layout — your dishwasher may differ.]
Filter is fairly clean, nothing blocking it. Can't say about the sump, I didn't look at that. Is there any way to deal with the water in the base tray without pulling the machine out?

There is no safe way for you to remove that water from the base tray without moving or tilting the machine. The anti-float switch sits at the very bottom, and if it stays wet, the pump will keep running and the error will not clear. Since we cannot access the base, we need to determine why the water got there in the first place. Please check inside the tub: with the filter removed, is there standing water in the sump that is more than a small cupful? If you see significant water or debris under the pump cover, sponge it out and let me know what you find.
I haven't looked in the sump yet. I'll check it now, but if it's not that, is there anything else I can do without pulling the machine out?

Before you start, switch it off and unplug it. To answer your question directly: no, there is no way to remove that water from the base tray without moving or tilting the machine. The anti-flood switch sits at the very bottom of the appliance, and as long as it stays wet, the pump will keep running and the error will not clear. Since you cannot access the base pan to drain it yourself, this is a job for an engineer. They have the tools to safely remove the machine or access the sump from underneath (if possible) to drain the tray and investigate the source of the leak (often a failing pump seal or internal hose). Please contact your appliance repair service or manufacturer support to arrange a visit.
